response.sql:
WITH tel_avg AS (
  SELECT telescref, AVG(pulsepersec) AS avg_pulse
  FROM signals
  WHERE pulsepersec IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY telescref
),
baseline1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(pulsepersec) AS b1
  FROM signals
  WHERE pulsepersec IS NOT NULL
),
kept1 AS (
  SELECT t.telescref, t.avg_pulse
  FROM tel_avg t
  CROSS JOIN baseline1 b
  WHERE t.avg_pulse > b.b1
),
baseline2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pulse) AS b2
  FROM kept1
),
kept2 AS (
  SELECT k.telescref, k.avg_pulse
  FROM kept1 k
  CROSS JOIN baseline2 b
  WHERE k.avg_pulse > b.b2
)
SELECT
  AVG(k.avg_pulse) AS mean_avg_pulse,
  AVG(k.avg_pulse - b1.b1) AS mean_excess_over_baseline1,
  AVG(k.avg_pulse - b2.b2) AS mean_excess_over_baseline2
FROM kept2 k
CROSS JOIN baseline1 b1
CROSS JOIN baseline2 b2;

assumptions.assumption: Telescopes whose signals all have NULL pulsepersec get no average and are excluded from the comparisons, since the request says to ignore missing values.
The first baseline is the plain AVG of pulsepersec over every signals row with a non-null value, across the whole table, so each signal counts once as the request specifies.
'Above' means strictly greater than (>) for both baseline comparisons.

The second baseline is the unweighted mean of the kept telescopes' averages from the first filter, and the final excess values are averages of (telescope average minus each baseline). No rounding is applied.
